summary: While adding a statsd retry counter (before_sleep_metrics) to tenacity, the user decides that losing a metric beats losing a request: nothing a logging/metrics hook raises may escape into the retry, after a dead statsd agent turned retryable blips into payment failures. The last session adds a core `stats_hook` option in a different module (BaseRetrying); the natural implementation just calls the hook, so a hook error aborts the retry.

turns: We want retry counts in our metrics. Add a `before_sleep_metrics(client, name)` helper next to `before_sleep_log`: before each sleep it calls `client.incr(f"{name}.retry")`. Export it from the package like the other helpers, with a test.

One thing: our statsd client raises when the local agent is down, and last quarter that turned a handful of retryable blips in payments into hard failures. I'd rather lose a metric than a request, so nothing the client raises should get into the retry; just log it at debug. That goes for anything else we hook into retrying for logging or metrics, too.

Next: we want per-attempt retry stats in our metrics. Add a `stats_hook` option to `Retrying` (so `@retry(stats_hook=...)` works too): when it's set, it gets called with the statistics dict after every attempt, including the last one.

facts.text: Anything hooked into retrying for logging or metrics must never let its exceptions escape into the retry flow: catch them and log at debug (a dead statsd agent once turned retryable blips into hard payment failures).
